Memory for: Why does the Workbench's whole-space lint check never run on its own?
[1] Workbench/Maintenance.md (Space-wide lint)
  Space-wide lint: The space-wide lint runs [[API/space#space.lint]] over every page. This reads each page, runs every lint rule and renders its `${…}` expressions and Lua widgets, so on a large space it can take a while. That’s why it never runs by itself: press **Run space-wide lint** when you want it.
  The Maintenance tab lists (potential) problems in your space in one place. / ${widgets.commandButton("Workbench: Maintenance")} opens this tab in the [[Workbench]]. / The checks below are instant, and refresh as your space changes: / * **Broken links:** links to pages that don’t exist yet ([[Tag/aspiring-page|aspiring pages]]). / * **Ambiguous links:** links that could mean more than one page (see [[Link#Ambiguous links]]). / * **Scripts and styles:** scripts that failed to load or are quarantined, and styles that hold CSS the browser parsed no rules from. / * **Merge conflicts:** unresolved merges that need your decision.
[2] Workbench/Libraries.md (Checking for updates)
  The Libraries tab manages the [[Library|libraries]] in your space. In a read-only space it only shows what’s there: installing, updating, removing and checking for updates are hidden, with a note saying why (a read-only server doesn’t reach other servers, so there is nothing to check against). It reloads every time you show the tab, so what you see matches your space. / ${widgets.commandButton("Workbench: Libraries")} opens this tab in the [[Workbench]]. / The toolbar has: / * **Filter libraries**: narrows installed libraries by name and available ones by name, description and page. / * **Install…**: asks for a library or plug URI (`https://…` or `github:…`) and installs it. For a plug (a URI ending in `.plug.js`) it also asks where to save it.
[3] Workbench.md (Workbench)
  * [[Workbench/Libraries|Libraries]]: install, update and remove [[Library|libraries]] and [[Repository|repositories]], and check what has an update. / * [[Workbench/Maintenance|Maintenance]]: problems in your space, such as broken links, failed scripts, merge conflicts and (on demand) lint errors. / * [[Workbench/Console|Console]]: everything your space logs, plus a [[Space Lua]] REPL.
[4] CLI.md (Installation)
  Space Lua and Space Style pages: A `write` or `edit` of a Markdown page that has, or had, `space-lua` or `space-style` blocks makes the space reload its scripts and styles, so the change takes effect at once, then reports that page’s load errors and lint problems (the same check as [[API/space#space.lint]]) on stderr. With `--json` they are in the result’s `reload` field: `status` (`clean`, `problems`, `failed` or `no_runtime`), `loadErrors` and `lint`. A write that reports problems still happened: stderr says so, and the command exits with code 9 so a script notices. Fix the page and write it again.
